chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from Zurara, who said:
He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with buying the land of the Ahl al-Dhimma (people of the covenant) when they cultivate it and revive it, so it is for them.

key_terms.أَحْيَوْهَا: They revived it (brought it back to productive use)
key_terms.أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ: People of the covenant (non-Muslims living under Islamic rule)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy land from non-Muslims if they have cultivated it?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Zurara, clarifies the permissibility of purchasing agricultural land from Ahl al-Dhimma provided they have actively cultivated and revived it, thereby establishing their ownership rights. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the principle of 'ihya al-mawat' (reviving dead land) and validates private property rights within the dhimmi community under Islamic governance. It serves as a foundational text for understanding economic interactions and land tenure systems in classical Islamic society.
